fields.label: Show Application Reason on Attendance Sheet Hover
fields.description: When enabled, hovering a Late Entry, Early Exit, Out of Office, Attendance Request, or Leave Application in the Monthly Attendance Sheet BS popup shows the reason.

fields.label: Enable Late Entry & Early Exit Penalty Rules

fields.description: When enabled, a day covered by a submitted and approved Attendance Request is fully excused: no Late Entry / Early Exit flag, no occurrence-pool count, and no ½P / 1P penalty. Late and early minutes are still recorded for reference. When disabled, late and early are decided only from the actual check-in and check-out times, regardless of any Attendance Request.
fields.label: Approved Attendance Request Excuses Late / Early

fields.description: Minutes after shift start / before shift end that are free. No application needed; no pool count and no half-day deduction within this window.
fields.label: Grace Minutes

fields.description: Maximum delay still treated as a minor (pool) late/early. Between grace and this value: counts toward the monthly pool if no approved application. Beyond this value: immediate half-day (unless covered by half-day leave / Office Work).
fields.label: Max Delay Minutes

fields.description: Number of free late/early occurrences in the grace→max band (no application) before the first half-day. Example: 2 means first 2 free, 3rd deducts half-day.
fields.label: Initial Grace Occurrences

fields.description: If enabled, late and early pool occurrences share one combined monthly tally for half-day / full-day penalties.
fields.label: Combine Late & Early Occurrence Pool

fields.description: If unexcused late/early pool count in the payroll month is greater than this number, deduct full-day absent instead of half-day for the occurrence penalties.
fields.label: Full-Day Absent After Pool Occurrences

fields.description: After a half-day penalty from the pool, this many further occurrences are free before the next half-day. Example: 2 means two free, then another half-day.
fields.label: Subsequent Grace Step Occurrences

fields.description: When enabled, if the monthly unexcused late/early pool count is greater than the threshold below, occurrence penalties are deducted as full-day absent (gross) instead of half-day (basic).
fields.label: Enable Full-Day Absent Escalation

fields.description: An approved Personal Work slip explains the delay but does not make it company time, so the occurrence still counts toward the pool and can earn a ½P in the usual way. Leave this off to excuse an approved slip outright, whatever the type of work. Office Work is always fully excused.
fields.label: Count Approved Personal Work Toward the Pool

fields.description: When enabled, Late Entry, Early Exit and Out of Office Applications must be filed within the max days below after the attendance date.
fields.label: Enable Application Submission Deadline

fields.description: Max days after the attendance date to submit a Late Entry, Early Exit or Out of Office Application. Example: 2 means the form must be filed within 2 days of that attendance date. The Leave Submission Deadline uses the same window, measured from the leave's end date.
fields.label: Max Days to Submit Application

fields.description: When enabled, a Leave Application filed more than the max days below after its own end date is blocked. Leave types listed beside this stay open indefinitely -- sickness is rarely known in advance.
fields.label: Enable Leave Submission Deadline

fields.description: Leave types exempt from the deadline. Anything not listed is blocked once the window has passed.
fields.label: Leave Types Exempt from the Deadline

fields.description: Weekends and holidays that sit between full-day leave or absence are marked Absent and deducted on the salary slip (unapproved absence).
fields.label: Enable Leave Sandwich Rule
Block Leave Application on Sandwich Rule Violation

fields.description: These leave types appear as shortcuts on the BSHRMS leave form, with remaining balance. Other types stay in the dropdown.
fields.label: PWA Frequent Leave Types

fields.description: Shown as quick choices on the BSHRMS leave form. Only types allocated to the employee (or LWP) are listed. Remaining types stay in the dropdown.
fields.label: Frequent Leave Types
Max Paid Out of Office Hours Per Day

fields.description: ASR policy: when an approved Leave Without Pay application length is at or above the threshold, LWP days on the salary slip are deducted using gross daily rate instead of basic.
fields.label: Enable Continuous LWP Gross Deduction

fields.description: Per Leave Application length in days (to_date − from_date + 1). If any LWP application covering the payroll period is at least this many days, LWP deduction uses gross salary.
fields.label: Continuous LWP Threshold Days

fields.description: When enabled, employees cannot approve or submit their own Attendance Request. Their Leave Approver or HR must do it.
fields.label: Prevent Self-Approval of Attendance Requests

fields.description: When enabled, employees cannot approve or reject their own OOO Work check-ins.
fields.label: Prevent Self-Approval of OOO Check-ins

fields.description: When enabled, employees cannot approve, reject, or submit their own Late Entry, Early Exit, or Out of Office Application.
fields.label: Prevent Self-Approval of CNR Applications

fields.description: Control which roles can use BSHRMS PWA attendance and leave-board features. Empty tables turn that feature off; Leave Board also inherits Live Attendance Board roles.
fields.label: PWA Boards

fields.description: Roles allowed to see the Live Attendance Board. Empty means nobody.
fields.label: Live Attendance Board Roles

fields.description: Roles allowed to see leave boards. Live Attendance Board roles also have access.
fields.label: Leave Board Roles

fields.description: Roles allowed to browse historical attendance for other employees. Own attendance history remains available.
fields.label: Calendar Past Attendance Roles

fields.description: Roles allowed to view other employees' attendance calendars.
fields.label: View Others' Calendar Roles

fields.description: Watermark for the monthly BS leave allocation job. Do not confuse with the current BS date held in Nepal Compliance Settings.
fields.label: Last BS Allocation Year

fields.description: How a monthly salary is converted to a per-day rate for absence, LWP, late and OOO deductions. Fixed Days - always divide by the number below (Nepali practice is 30). Same deduction for the same absence in every month. Days in Payroll Period - the actual length of the slip's period, so a 29-day period divides by 29. Days in BS Month - the true length of the Bikram Sambat month the period starts in (29 to 32 days). Working Days in Period - the slip's Total Working Days, i.e. excluding holidays and weekly offs. This makes each absent day cost the most.
fields.label: Daily Rate Basis
fields.options:
Fixed Days
Days in Payroll Period
Days in BS Month
Working Days in Period

fields.description: Divisor used when the basis is Fixed Days.
fields.label: Fixed Days

fields.description: Choose which monthly salary amount is divided by the Daily Rate Basis for each attendance deduction.
fields.label: Attendance Deduction Bases

fields.description: Used for late entry, early exit and out-of-office half-days. The selected daily amount is divided by two.
fields.label: Half-Day Deduction Base
fields.options:
Basic Salary Only
Basic Salary + Grade
Basic Salary + Dearness Allowance
Basic Salary + Grade + Dearness Allowance
Basic Remuneration (SSF/PF Base)
Total Fixed Remuneration (Gross)
Assignment Base (Total Salary)

fields.description: Used for each unapproved absent day and escalated full-day late or early-exit penalty.
fields.label: Unapproved Absence Deduction Base
fields.options:
Basic Salary Only
Basic Salary + Grade
Basic Salary + Dearness Allowance
Basic Salary + Grade + Dearness Allowance
Basic Remuneration (SSF/PF Base)
Total Fixed Remuneration (Gross)
Assignment Base (Total Salary)

fields.description: Normal Leave Without Pay rate. Continuous LWP and Period Leave Gross LWP can still switch this to Gross after their thresholds.
fields.label: LWP Deduction Base
fields.options:
Basic Salary Only
Basic Salary + Grade
Basic Salary + Dearness Allowance
Basic Salary + Grade + Dearness Allowance
Basic Remuneration (SSF/PF Base)
Total Fixed Remuneration (Gross)
Assignment Base (Total Salary)

fields.description: Base for late / early occurrence-pool penalties (½P counts 0.5 day, 1P counts 1.0 day). Leave blank to keep charging them on the Half-Day Deduction Base.
fields.label: Penalty Deduction Base
fields.options:
Basic Salary Only
Basic Salary + Grade
Basic Salary + Dearness Allowance
Basic Salary + Grade + Dearness Allowance
Basic Remuneration (SSF/PF Base)
Total Fixed Remuneration (Gross)
Assignment Base (Total Salary)

fields.label: Payroll Year Opening Period
fields.description: Payroll cycles need not begin on the first day of a BS month. The payroll year's opening slip is the only one with no earlier slip to carry its leading days, so they reach no slip at all.

fields.label: Extend the Payroll Year's Opening Period
fields.description: Count the payroll year's first Salary Slip from the day its cycle actually begins, so working days, leave, absence and penalties cover the span the Monthly Attendance Sheet BS reports. The cycle's first day is read from the slip's own end date and the opening month from the Payroll Period or Fiscal Year covering it; later periods in the year are never changed.
Controls whether the complete attendance deduction (late entry, early exit, out of office, LWP and unapproved absence) reduces earned salary components instead of posting as a separate deduction.
fields.label: Earned Salary Attendance Deductions

fields.description: Show contractual and earned amounts side by side, reduce salary earnings by the attendance amount, and keep Leave and Late Deduction as an informational row excluded from totals and accounting. Disable this to retain the legacy fixed-earnings plus actual-deduction behavior.
fields.label: Calculate Attendance Deductions Through Earned Salary

fields.description: When unchecked, deduct non-contribution allowances first and reduce Basic only if those allowances are exhausted. When checked, spread the deduction proportionally across Basic, Dearness Allowance, Grade and other fixed allowances; SSF/PF/Gratuity then use the reduced contribution base.
fields.label: Reduce Basic and Allowances Proportionally

fields.description: Controls the Nepal Standard Salary Slip print format. These options change presentation only; they do not affect payroll calculations or accounting.
fields.label: Salary Slip Print

fields.description: Employee field whose value is printed as Employee ID. The dropdown is populated from Employee fields, including custom Data and Link fields.
fields.label: Employee ID Source Field

fields.description: Show the employee's bank name and account number at the bottom of the salary slip.
fields.label: Show Bank Details

fields.description: Selected earning components appear in a separate half-width Additional Earnings table and are excluded from the Monthly Earnings table.
fields.label: Additional Earnings

fields.description: When enabled, if LWP + absent days in the payroll period are more than the threshold, all LWP on the slip is deducted at the Gross daily rate instead of the LWP Deduction Base. Paid leave is not counted.
fields.label: Enable Period Leave Gross LWP

fields.description: If LWP + absent days in this payroll period are more than this number, LWP is deducted from Gross. Paid leave is not counted. Example: 5 means 6 or more LWP/absent days trigger Gross. This is separate from Continuous LWP, which looks at one application's length.
fields.label: Period Leave Threshold Days

fields.description: How the Salary Structure Assignment breakdown converts to pay. Base always equals Basic + Dearness Allowance + Grade + Other Allowances.
fields.label: Contribution & Overtime

fields.description: When only Base is entered (e.g. via Bulk Salary Structure Assignment), Basic Salary is derived as this percent of Base and the remainder becomes Other Allowance. SSF requires basic to be at least 60% of remuneration.
fields.label: Default Basic Salary %

fields.description: Grade increments are normally treated as basic remuneration. Uncheck only if your SSF registration says otherwise.
fields.label: Include Grade in SSF / PF / Gratuity Base

fields.description: Overtime is paid at this multiple of the normal hourly rate. Labour Act 2074 s.31 sets 1.5x, and caps overtime at 4 hours a day / 24 hours a week. Baked into the Overtime formula when you run Setup.
fields.label: Overtime Rate Multiplier

fields.description: Off by default: DA is part of the statutory minimum wage but is not normally part of basic remuneration for contribution purposes.
fields.label: Include Dearness Allowance in SSF / PF / Gratuity Base

fields.description: Suggested Leave Encashment Per Day formula for new Salary Structure Assignments. Assignments can override it. Clearing the Assignment formula does not re-lock it to this value on save.
fields.label: Leave Encashment

fields.description:
Pre-fills Salary Structure Assignment → Leave Encashment Formula when that field is empty. Edit freely on each Assignment.

Available names include: base, custom_basic_remuneration (alias basic_remuneration), custom_basic_salary, custom_dearness_allowance, custom_grade_amount, custom_total_fixed_remuneration, custom_total_allowances, nsa_<abbr>, and Salary Structure component abbrs.

Example: custom_basic_remuneration / 30
fields.label: Default Leave Encashment Formula

fields.description: Defines the period a payroll run covers. Used to suggest dates on Payroll Entry and Salary Slip, and to resolve per-period day overrides. To change the day count for one month only — for example treating Shrawan as 32 days instead of 31 — create a Nepal Payroll Period Override. Overrides carry an Applies From date and are snapshotted onto each salary slip when it is first calculated, so existing slips keep the divisor they were computed with.
fields.label: Attendance & Payroll Period

fields.description: Nepali Month - the period runs from day 1 to the last day of the BS month. Custom Day Range - the period straddles two BS months, e.g. the 29th of one to the 28th of the next.
fields.label: Payroll Period Basis

fields.description: BS day the period opens on. 29 means the period runs from the 29th of one month to the 28th of the next. Must be between 1 and 29 (every BS month has at least 29 days).
fields.label: Period Start Day (BS)

fields.description: Fixed by the Minimum Remuneration Fixation Committee and revised every two years. Nepal states the minimum as Basic + Dearness Allowance separately, so both floors are enforced independently as well as on the total.
fields.label: Government Minimum Wage

fields.description: आधारभूत तलब floor. The basic half of the statutory minimum wage. Note: your existing Basic Salary formula hardcodes 12170 - set whichever figure is current.
fields.label: Minimum Monthly Basic Salary

fields.description: Combined floor. Basic + Dearness Allowance on an assignment must reach this, on top of each component clearing its own floor above.
fields.label: Minimum Monthly Remuneration

fields.description: महँगी भत्ता floor. The DA half of the statutory minimum wage.
fields.label: Minimum Monthly Dearness Allowance

fields.description: Maps each kind of payroll posting to a GL account, per company. Running Setup assigns these to every Salary Component it creates, so you do not have to open each component to set its account. Wages and Salary are separate purposes because they post to different expense accounts.
fields.label: Component Account Mapping

fields.description: An Additional Salary raised against the wrong variant pays the right amount but posts to the wrong expense account. The component picker already hides the opposite variant; this covers records created by import or API.
fields.label: Component Variant Check

fields.description: What to do when an Additional Salary names a Wages component for an employee on a Salary structure, or the reverse. Block - refuse to save, naming the component to use instead. Warn - show the message and save anyway. Components with no variant suffix (TDS, CIT, Insurance, SSF and PF) post to liability accounts and are never flagged.
fields.label: On Variant Mismatch

fields.description: Creates a Payroll Entry per salary structure on a chosen day of the BS month, for the period that just ended. Runs from the daily scheduler, so the site's scheduler must be enabled.
fields.label: Automated Payroll Runs

fields.description: BS day of the month the job fires on. 1 means it runs on the first day of the new month and covers the month that just ended. Keep it at 28 or below so it exists in every BS month.
fields.label: Run on BS Day

fields.description: Create Payroll Entry Only - a draft with employees filled in, for someone to review. Safest. ...and Salary Slips - also creates draft slips. ...and Submit Salary Slips - also submits the slips, which posts the accrual journal entry. Nothing is ever submitted without this set explicitly.
fields.label: How Far to Go
fields.options:
Create Payroll Entry Only
Create Payroll Entry and Salary Slips
Create, and Submit Salary Slips

fields.description: Users with this role get a notification with the result of each run, including failures.
fields.label: Notify Role

fields.description: Runs the rows above immediately for the period that just ended, ignoring the day check. Useful for a dry run before relying on the scheduler.
fields.label: Run Scheduled Payroll Now

fields.description: One row per Payroll Entry to create each period. Typically one per salary structure, e.g. a Wages row and a Salary row.
fields.label: Scheduled Runs

fields.description: Creates the Nepal salary components, four salary structures (SSF and PF/Gratuity, each in a Wages and a Salary variant), and the income tax slab — then applies the account mapping above. Safe to re-run: existing records are updated, never duplicated. Structures already on the site are left untouched.
fields.label: Payroll Setup

fields.description: The bot that posts attendance alerts. Pick an existing Raven Bot or create one named Nepal HRMS (reused if it already exists).
fields.label: Raven Bot

fields.description: Name of an existing Raven Bot.
fields.label: Raven Bot

fields.description: Created on save if it does not already exist.
fields.label: New Bot Name

fields.description: Default channel for events that have Channel checked but do not pick their own. Creating it also adds the bot and users who have the roles below (only if they are already Raven Users).
fields.label: Raven Channel

fields.description: Raven Channel document name (not the display title).
fields.label: Raven Channel

fields.description: Raven Workspace to create the channel in. Defaults to Raven if left empty.
fields.label: Workspace

fields.description: Users with these roles who are already Raven Users are added to the channel on each save.
fields.label: Channel Member Roles
BSHRMS PWA
fields.description: The mobile app is a separate delivery channel from Raven and needs neither a bot nor a channel. It notifies the employee's own user, so nobody has to be a Raven User to receive one.

fields.label: Enable PWA Notifications
fields.description: Master switch for the BSHRMS PWA. Off until you turn it on, and off stops every PWA notification at once without disturbing the per-event boxes or the Raven side. Each event still needs its own PWA box ticked below.

One list for both channels: each row picks who is notified, then whether it goes to Raven, the PWA, or both. Raven direct messages are skipped when the person is not a Raven User; PWA notifications are not. All events start disabled.
fields.label: Attendance Notifications
